summary.text: 去 commonly means “go away,” “leave,” or “depart.” Its early graph is disputed: one interpretation sees a person leaving an opening, while another identifies a covered vessel. The evidence does not settle what the graph originally depicted.

formation.text: The early graph’s construction is disputed. One interpretation reads a person above an opening and connects the scene with departure; another identifies a covered vessel and relates the graph to 盍. Shuowen parses it as 大 plus phonetic 凵, but the vessel-cover analysis contests that parsing. A proposed connection to 呿, “open the mouth,” remains unproven. The proposed path from covering to departure is an interpretation, not a documented sequence.

history.text: The recorded forms include oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, and Shuowen small-seal examples. The oracle redraw has a narrow upper stroke with branching arms above an enclosed lower shape; the small-seal form has an open-bottom enclosure. These forms are described from source records, and their shapes do not settle what the earlier graph depicts.

Shuowen explains 去 as people parting and parses it as 大 plus 凵, with 凵 as the sound element. A separate interpretation reads a person leaving a cave opening. Yang and Sun instead identify the oracle graph as an early form of 盍 and cite a bronze form of 盍 analyzed as 去 plus 皿. These are competing accounts of the graph’s history.

uncertainties.text: The early graph has been read as a person and opening or as a covered vessel. Departure is not securely established in the oracle-bone examples discussed, and the proposed connection from covering to departure is not a documented sequence.
A proposal connects 去 with 呿, “open the mouth,” but the evidence does not establish 呿 as the source of 去’s original sound or meaning. Later reading relationships do not prove that origin.

senses.period: Western Zhou (as characterized for transmitted Zhouyi and Shijing passages; exact manuscript dating unresolved)
senses.text: The cited departure uses occur in transmitted Zhouyi and Shijing passages characterized as Western Zhou usage; the quoted lines are not independently dated manuscript attestations. Departure is not securely established in the oracle-bone examples discussed.

senses.gloss: put away; eliminate; get rid of
senses.text: Historical reading records associate 去 with “get rid of” as well as “depart” and distinguish readings for these uses, but do not establish when they arose or how they are related.
In current use, 去 commonly means “go away,” “leave,” or “depart.”

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish whether “get rid of” developed from “depart,” the reverse, or represents a separate historical use. Departure is also not securely established in the oracle-bone examples discussed.
The proposed ancient readings do not provide an independently established sound comparison proving borrowing from 呿 or identifying the pronunciation of the object depicted in the early graph.
